role.altitude: The driver's week is still the road: the load, the truck and the route. Less of it is re-keying a bill or hunting a scrap note. A mismatch on the loaded goods, a vehicle that may be unsafe, and whether the trailer fits stay with the driver. The planner holds a damaged vehicle or a clashing instruction.
reach: Light truck drivers: the same note check and the same short defect report, on a smaller vehicle
Bus drivers: a proposed line on a screen is not the decision to divert
skills_to_grow: Tell a note-field mismatch from goods that are actually wrong
State only the approved incident facts when a notice leaves the firm
Refuse a proposed route the vehicle cannot take
role.ambitious_version: The assignment and the site instruction are on the transport order before departure. A doubtful paper note is compared once. A defect is a short account. The driver still decides if the truck and the road are safe.

tasks.short: Read the bill of lading and determine the assignment details.

steps.what: Read bills of lading to determine the assignment details.
Photograph a paper lading note the shipper still hands over.
Compare photographed lading fields with the transport order.

loop.input: The photo of the paper note and the transport order
loop.output: A field comparison a person can read
loop.check: The check confirms the consignee name, the weight and the reference on the photo match the order, not only that an identifier exists
loop.stop: One pass, or stop when a field is unreadable and hand the photo to the driver
loop.why_not_simpler: A rules check cannot read a foreign paper note

steps.what: Flag assignment details that do not match the loaded goods.
Hold or release the load when the lading details clash.

tasks.design: {OPS_SYSTEM} shows the assignment from the electronic consignment note. A paper note from a foreign shipper is photographed once on the phone ({OTHER}); a bounded read compares consignee, weight and reference with the transport order, and a mismatch goes to the planner. The driver still checks the seal, the count and the loaded goods.
tasks.previous_blocker: Foreign shippers still hand over a paper note, and a rules check cannot read it. The driver was the only person who could put those fields next to the order.
tasks.enabler_now: The electronic note can already be issued inside the transport system, and one bounded read can pull fields off a photo and compare them with that order.
tasks.still_hard: Handwriting, a wet page and a note in an unexpected layout still fail the read. The walk around the trailer does not get shorter because the fields matched.
tasks.human_edge: The driver sees whether the seal, the count and the goods match the assignment. The planner decides whether a clash holds the load.
tasks.altitude: The driver still starts from the bill, but spends less of the stop re-keying fields that are already on the order. The right to hold a clashing load stays with the planner; the right to say the goods do not match stays with the driver.

reach.task: Read a consignment note to see the load assignment
reach.learn: The same field check works on a smaller truck when the note is on the transport order. The physical check of the goods does not transfer to a screen.

evidence.claim: An electronic consignment note can be created, issued and signed inside a transport system, and that note is the record used when someone reads and checks load documents.
A Dutch grocer started electronic consignment notes in 2021 with three carriers. That shows firms already issue them. It does not measure how many minutes a driver spends reading one.
Authorities must accept certified electronic freight-information platform data from 9 July 2027. They need not accept it today.
Abroad, a driver may still need a paper consignment note.
Matching fields on a note does not replace the driver's check of the seal, the count and the loaded goods.

assumptions: The prior that puts about two thirds of this task in meetings is the driver reading a note in the cab or at the dock, not a meeting. The steps treat that time as a document.
The machine step is only the field comparison of a photographed paper note. The walk around the load stays in the flag step at about two thirds of today's time.
Eight hours per 100 baseline hours is the driver's steady upkeep when a photo is unreadable or a field match is wrong. It is not zero, and it is not the build.
unknowns: What share of this firm's bills are already electronic, and which lanes still require a paper note.
Whether a photo of a note taken on the phone is stored with the driver's location.
research_questions: On a typical week, how many bills are electronic, how many are a foreign paper note, and how many clash with the goods?

already_counted.description: The driver still reads the assignment on the note or the order.
The driver still photographs the paper note when a shipper hands one over.
The driver still flags goods that do not match the assignment.

incremental.description: Fix unreadable photos and wrong field matches on paper notes.
Planner samples clashing notes beyond the hold-or-release call.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of electronic notes and few foreign paper bills lands near 42 percent of driver time on this task, because reading and the field comparison shrink while the load check stays. A week of foreign paper notes and frequent mismatches lands near 18, because the photo, the driver's flag and the planner's hold stay. Both sit under the central net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report vehicle defects, accidents, traffic violations or damage.

steps.what: Notice vehicle defects, accidents, traffic violations or damage.
Write the defect, accident or damage into the vehicle report.
Call the planner when the vehicle cannot safely continue.
Decide whether the vehicle is grounded and the notice can go out.
Send the approved accident or violation notice outside the firm.

tasks.design: The driver still notices defects, accidents, traffic violations and damage, and still decides if the vehicle can move. A short report on {OPS_SYSTEM} replaces the paper form. A notice that leaves the firm goes out only after the transport planner has approved that exact snapshot. The form stores place and time only with works-council consent, and it does not score the driver.
tasks.previous_blocker: The report was a paper form or a phone call, and an outside notice mixed the driver's account with a decision about whether the vehicle was safe to move.
tasks.enabler_now: The transport system can hold a short structured report. The planner's yes can bind one snapshot before anything is sent outside.
tasks.still_hard: Saying whether the truck is safe to move, and telling an authority what happened, stays a person's account. A form does not see the damage.
tasks.human_edge: The driver is at the vehicle and is responsible for not moving an unsafe one. The planner decides grounding and whether the notice leaves the firm.
tasks.altitude: The driver still owns the first look at the truck and the call when it cannot continue. Writing the same facts takes less of the stop. Sending a notice outside is no longer the driver's own decision.

reach.task: Report a defect or accident on a smaller vehicle
reach.learn: The short report and the planner's yes before an outside notice transfer. The judgement that the vehicle is unsafe does not.

evidence.claim: A short structured report can cut the time spent writing the same facts. It does not decide whether the vehicle is safe to move.
Telematics and a driver app observe location and behaviour. In the Netherlands the works council's consent applies under WOR article 27, and GDPR applies to that data.
Scoring drivers, or allocating work by behaviour, falls under Annex III point 4(b). This design does not score drivers or rank who filed a report.
France's CNIL fined Amazon France Logistique 32 million euro in December 2023 for scanner indicators of exact idle time and for keeping them 31 days. This design does not add idle-time indicators.

assumptions: The prior that puts most of this task in meetings is the driver at the vehicle or on the phone, not a meeting. Noticing damage stays in person. The report today is a paper form, which matches the prior that standard software usually does not cover it.

Four hours per 100 baseline hours is the driver correcting a report that stored the wrong place or the wrong damage line. Planner sampling of reports is other-role time and is not taken off the driver's saving.
No per-driver score and no idle-time indicator are in this design. If the form stores location, consent comes first.
unknowns: Which notices must go to an authority, and which stay inside the firm.
Whether the current report already captures location, and whether the works council has already consented.
research_questions: What share of defect reports are a paper form, a phone call, or both, and what share become a notice that leaves the firm?

already_counted.description: The driver still reviews the vehicle report before it is stored.
The driver still calls the planner when the vehicle cannot continue.
The driver still sends the notice after the planner has approved that snapshot.

incremental.description: Correct a report that stored the wrong place, time or damage line.
Planner samples incident reports beyond the grounding decision.

approvals.approved_version: Vehicle incident report snapshot with place, time, the defect or damage description, and the planner's yes to send that snapshot

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When most of the stop is noticing the damage and calling because the vehicle cannot continue, saving stays near 4 percent of driver time on this task. When the written report is the main cut and an outside notice is rare, it stays near 14. Noticing the defect and the safety call barely shrink. Both figures sit under the central net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect delivery instructions and verify them against the routes.

steps.what: Publish delivery instructions onto the transport order.
Collect delivery instructions from the appropriate sources.
Read a delivery instruction that arrived by phone or a scrap note.
Keep verifying delivery instructions against the planned routes.

loop.input: The free-text shipper note, the written instruction and the planned route
loop.output: A stated clash on height, time window or site access, or a statement that none is present
loop.check: The check confirms the clash names a real restriction in the note, such as a height, a time window or an access rule, and the route it conflicts with, not only that a note identifier exists
loop.stop: One pass. If the note is unreadable the driver verifies it without the draft.
loop.why_not_simpler: A rules check cannot read an unstructured shipper note

steps.what: Call the site when verifying the route still leaves a clash.
Site contact states the access rule the instruction left out.

tasks.design: Standard delivery instructions are published on the transport order in {OPS_SYSTEM} before departure, and the driver collects them there. A free-text shipper note is read once and set against the planned routes for a height, a time window or an access clash. The driver still verifies a clash and calls the site on {TELEPHONY}. A paper note abroad stays a document the driver reads.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions arrived as a phone call, a scrap note or a line buried in a message, so the driver had to collect them before anyone could see a clash with the route.
tasks.enabler_now: The transport order can hold the standard instruction before departure, and one bounded read can name a clash in a free-text note. The driver still confirms it.
tasks.still_hard: A site that changes access on the day, and a note that names a local ban the order does not know, still need a person on the phone.
tasks.human_edge: The driver confirms that a stated clash is real for this vehicle and this arrival. The site contact is the person who knows the access rule the instruction missed.
tasks.altitude: The driver spends less of the departure hunting for a scrap note when the instruction is already on the order. Verifying a clash, and the call to the site, stay with the driver. No new decision right moves to the driver.

reach.task: Collect a delivery instruction before a drop
reach.learn: Publishing the instruction on the order helps a smaller vehicle too. Site access still needs a person.

evidence.claim: An electronic consignment note created inside a transport system can carry the written instruction the driver reads. It does not cover a site note that arrives later by phone.
Abroad, a driver may still need a paper note, so a phone or scrap instruction does not disappear on every lane.

A free-text shipper note still needs a person to confirm that a height, a time window or an access line really clashes with the route. No source in the digest measures how long drivers spend collecting instructions.

assumptions: The prior that puts most of this task in meetings is the driver collecting a note at the cab or the gate, not a meeting. Written instructions are a document. A phone change stays a phone call.
Five hours per 100 baseline hours is the driver correcting a misread note. The site contact's time is customer time and is not taken off the driver's saving.
The invoice-speed case in the digest is about invoices, not about collecting delivery instructions, so it is not used here.
unknowns: What share of instructions are on the order before departure, and what share still arrive as a phone call on the day.
Which lanes still require the paper note abroad.
research_questions: How often does a free-text note name a height, a time window or an access rule that the planned route cannot meet?

already_counted.description: The driver still reads the delivery instruction on the order before departing.
The driver still reviews the draft clash against the planned route.
The driver still calls the site when a clash remains.

incremental.description: Correct a note the read mis-stated, then verify the route again.
Site contact repeats an access rule the instruction left out.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of instructions already on the order lands near 20 percent of driver time on this task, because collecting them shrinks and the site call stays. A week of phone changes and scrap notes lands near 8, because verifying and the call to the site stay. Both sit under the central net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read and interpret maps to determine vehicle routes.

steps.what: Read the proposed vehicle route on the paper map sheet.
Interpret the proposed maps for vehicle routes a truck cannot take.
Show the latest legal break point on the driving-time display.
Determine which vehicle route the driver will actually drive.
Tell the planner when the vehicle route must change.

tasks.design: The cab route screen ({OTHER}) shows a proposed vehicle route taken from the transport order. The driver still interprets bans, height and whether the trailer fits, and still determines the route to drive. The driving-time display ({OTHER}) shows the latest legal break point so the driver does not calculate it by hand. The design does not score who followed the proposal.
tasks.previous_blocker: The route was a paper sheet or a map the driver read while judging height, weight and a local ban. No rule in the office could see the road in front of the truck.
tasks.enabler_now: The transport order can push a proposed route to the cab screen, and the tachograph display can show the latest legal break. Neither one chooses the road.
tasks.still_hard: A diversion, a low bridge and a trailer that does not fit the proposal stay the driver's call. Where the cab has no screen, the paper sheet stays.
tasks.human_edge: The driver is the person who can see that the proposed route is one this vehicle cannot take, and who remains responsible for the driving-time limits at the roadside.
tasks.altitude: The driver still chooses the road. Less of the choice is plotting a line on a paper sheet or working out the next break by hand. No decision right moves off the driver.

reach.task: Read a route and decide a diversion
reach.learn: A proposed line on a screen is not the decision. Height, weight and a trailer do not transfer to a bus.

evidence.claim: A cab screen can show a route the office proposed. The driver still judges height, weight and a local ban. No source in the digest measures map-reading time, and no navigation product is cited.
A tachograph tool can download records, archive them and raise a remaining-driving-time alert. On this task that alert is only the latest legal break point, not the choice of road.

Regulation 561/2006 limits driving to 9 hours a day, 10 hours twice a week, 56 hours a week and 90 hours in two weeks, with a 45-minute break after 4.5 hours. The driver remains responsible at the roadside.
A cab route that records location observes the driver. In the Netherlands the works council's consent applies under WOR article 27, and GDPR applies.
Scoring drivers or allocating work by behaviour falls under Annex III point 4(b). This design does not score who followed the proposed route.

assumptions: The prior that puts most of this task in meetings is the driver reading a map or watching the road, not a meeting. The route sheet today is a document. Standard software usually does not cover the interpretation.

Eight percent of the task today is glancing at the driving-time display to see when the next break falls. That glance is the only step marked machine. Interpretation of the map stays near all of today's time.

Two hours per 100 baseline hours is the driver correcting a proposal that ignored a restriction. Maintaining the restriction list is other-role time and is not taken off the driver's saving. Where there is no cab screen, the paper sheet stays and the low end of the range applies.
unknowns: Whether this fleet's cabs already show the office route, or only a paper sheet.
Whether storing the driven route against the proposal would be switched on. This design does not do that.
research_questions: What share of routes are a familiar trunk road, and what share are a diversion the driver has to interpret on the day?

already_counted.description: The driver still reads the proposed route on the sheet or the cab screen.
The driver still interprets which stretches this vehicle cannot take.
The driver still determines the route to drive after seeing the break deadline.

incremental.description: Correct a proposed route that ignored a height, a weight or a local ban.
Someone else maintains the restriction list the proposal uses.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a new diversion the driver still interprets the map, so saving stays near 5 percent of driver time on this task. On a familiar trunk route the paper plotting shrinks and the break is shown, so saving stays near 14, and the driver still chooses the road. Both sit under the central net. No digest source measures this time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
